t: This bronze statue of Henry Irving stands near the entrance of the National Portrait Gallery. It was unveiled on 5 December 1910, paid for by actors, actresses and others from British theatre. Thomas Brock was the sculptor, and the pedestal is Portland stone. Irving was a Victorian actor-manager who made his name at the Lyceum. He campaigned for theatre to be recognised as an art equal to music and painting, and in 1895 he became the first actor to be knighted. Each year on 6 February, the Irving Society lays a wreath here.
